thread:
Fern: Heads-up — spotted multiple drifts in the Colab quickstart and the accompanying Terraform sample. New hires hit reproducible issues in workshops today.
Fern: Colab notebook live snippet (copy/paste) shows: 
```python
# Cell 4
from redwood import ChatClient
client = ChatClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
resp = client.create_chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}])
print(resp)
```
Fern: Problems: (1) env var name `REDWOOD_KEY` is inconsistent with the rest of docs which use `REDWOOD_API_KEY`, (2) API surface is outdated — `ChatClient.create_chat` is from v0.8 and we've moved to `RedwoodClient.chat.create(...)`, (3) in runtime the kernel returns a coroutine object because the notebook runtime needs `await` (we should show `await client.chat.create(...)` inside an `asyncio` cell or use sync wrapper). New hires pasted this into Colab and got a `coroutine object` printed which confused them.
Avery: Also saw a Terraform snippet in infra/terraform/module.md that defines `variable "redwood_token" {}` while samples use `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Folks copy the var name into CI and nothing maps, so infra teams file tickets "missing variable redwood_api_key".
docs-bot: Snippet-linter findings: detected deprecated API usage pattern `ChatClient.create_chat` in docs/notebooks/colab/quickstart.ipynb, env var mismatch `REDWOOD_KEY`, and notebook async omission (printed coroutine) flagged. Rule IDs: nb-api-2026, nb-env-2026, nb-async-await-2026.
Jordan: Good catch. For Colab we should show two options: (A) minimal sync-friendly helper `from redwood import syncify; resp = syncify(client.chat.create)(...)` as a compact example, and (B) an async example with `import asyncio` and `await`. That way people using standard notebook cells won't be surprised.
Maya: I can patch the notebook to: (1) standardize to `os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')`, (2) replace old constructor with `client = RedwoodClient({ 'apiKey': os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY') })`, (3) add a short "Notebooks" note showing both syncify and async variants and mention top-level `await` availability in Colab by enabling the "Use IPython's asyncio" magic.
Fern: Nice. For the Terraform bit, we should clearly document that the module accepts `var.api_key` and map it in examples: `variable "api_key" {}` and then `module "redwood" { api_key = var.api_key }`. Standardize on `api_key` and mention the ENV var shape separately.
Kai: Can we also add a lint rule for notebooks that flags deprecated SDK call patterns (simple AST search) and env var names in code cells? I'd like to catch these during docs PRs rather than having them surface in workshops.
docs-bot: Suggestion accepted. Opening ticket DOCS-1234 to add notebook AST checks and env-var normalization to snippet-linter.
Jordan: I'll open a PR to update the Colab notebook and Terraform example. Plan: update text, add short migration note, and include a tiny smoke cell that asserts `os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY') is not None` only as an example (commented out) to avoid CI hitting prod.
Maya: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1123 - updates colab quickstart, normalizes env var, adds sync/async notebook examples, and fixes Terraform var names.
Fern: Sweet. After PR merges, let's ping the onboarding leads so they can refresh workshop materials. This would cut down several "why is this a coroutine" tickets we saw today.
Avery: Also recommending a short CONTRIBUTING note: "When editing notebooks, run `scripts/nb-sanity-check.sh` and confirm no deprecated SDK names appear in code cells." New contributors keep editing markdown only and miss code drift.
Jordan: Will add the script and the contributing note in the PR.
docs-bot: Preview deployed for PR #1123: https://docs.redwood.ai/pr-1123 - notebook-lint passes locally. :white_check_mark:
Fern: Thanks everyone — closing this thread after merge. :thumbsup:
